title: Opening principles (stub: outcomes only, no items yet)

D0.outcome: Names three opening principles with a reason each: take the centre, develop pieces before moving one twice, castle early.

D1.outcome: Given an early position and a short list of moves, chooses a developing move and says which principle it follows.

D2.outcome: Spots when an opening move breaks a principle and says what it costs (a piece left loose, a lost move), including when breaking it is fine.

D3.outcome: Explains, with a checked example for each, when each principle fails.

misconceptions: Principles are laws: breaking one always loses.
Developing means moving any piece, even the same one again and again.
conditions: Take the centre, develop pieces before moving one twice, castle early: each is a default with a reason, not a law.
A default holds only when following it leaves no piece loose and does not give the opponent time.
contrasts: A developing move that leaves a piece loose is not a good developing move.
Which flank you castle to does not decide whether castling early is a good idea.
